summary: Webpack loader fetches and shell-executes remote script from hardcoded IP, exfiltrates internal-network probe results
details: dist/bsrc-loader.js is a webpack loader entry reached via require('./bsrc-loader.js!./payload.txt') from renderer.umd.js, causing execution during any consumer's webpack build. On Linux, the loader spawns /bin/sh with a curl||wget pipeline that downloads http://180.76.53.183:80/slt and pipes the response into sh, running arbitrary attacker-controlled shell as the build user; it also spawns a detached 9-day sleeper via /bin/sh. Separately, the loader fetches http://bsrc-ssrf.n.baidu-int.com/bsrc_uid (an internal-network host) and sends the response body together with process.cwd(), the target root, and probe stdout/stderr, base64url-encoded, to http://49.232.169.67:80/bsrc-r273. The destination IP is assembled at runtime from the array ['49','232','169','67'].join('.') to evade literal-string detection. The combination of remote shell execution from a hardcoded IP, internal-network SSRF probing with results exfiltrated to an unrelated public IP, and split-string obfuscation of the C2 endpoint constitutes an installer-side remote code execution and data exfiltration payload.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
